chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The people have no leeway (for not doing so) until they ask, gain religious understanding, and recognize their Imam, and they have the capacity to take with what he says, even if it is under dissimulation (taqiyyah).

key_terms.إمامهم: Their Imam — specifically the divinely appointed Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.تقية: Taqiyyah — the practice of concealing one's beliefs or actions to avoid harm while maintaining internal fidelity
key_terms.يتفقهوا: To gain deep understanding of religion (fiqh), not merely surface knowledge
key_terms.يسع: To have leeway, to be permissible, to suffice — 'لا يسعهم' means they are not excused

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the obligation to recognize the Imam and follow his guidance under taqiyyah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that Muslims are obligated to seek knowledge, attain religious understanding, and recognize their Imam. This hadith emphasizes that obedience to the Imam's guidance is not optional — even when circumstances require that such adherence be practiced discreetly under taqiyyah. In the context of Abbasid persecution of the Shia, this teaching reinforced that believers must maintain their religious commitments and Imam-connection even under duress.
